Late / Absence Procedures
As in all schools within the Romsey Partnership of schools, we encourage a high level of attendance and punctuality.
Please click on the link to read the letter sent out in February 2024 to all Romsey parents: Joint Attendance Letter updated Feb 24- Primary
Regular and punctual attendance at school is a legal requirement. If your child is sick, please inform the school office promptly before 9am.
If you wish to take your child out of school for any other reason you will need to seek authorisation from the Headteacher. A form is available for this purpose in the school office. Holidays taken during term time will not be authorised but a form must still be completed so we know the whereabouts of your child.
If we do not know the whereabouts of your child, we will follow our safeguarding procedures which involve: truancy texts and calls, home visits or even reports to the Police.
If a Penalty Notice is issued, it is done so in accordance with Hampshire County Council’s Code of Conduct. Once issued is out of the hands of the school and dealt with by Hampshire County Council. Circumstances in which a penalty notice may be issued include:
If paid within 21 days of receipt of the Penalty Notice, the penalty is £60 per parent per child. If not paid within 21 days the penalty is automatically increased to £120 per parent per child to be paid within 28 days. It is likely that non payment will result in prosecution.
Any revenue resulting from payment of penalties will be retained by the County Council and is used to cover enforcement costs.

Wrap Around Care
Our Breakfast and After School clubs are a great facility and enjoyed by many. Breakfast Club is held in the school hall and After School Club is held in Hazel Nest. Access is through the main pedestrian gate on Nursling Street. For collection from After school club please phone our dedicated mobile phone.
The Breakfast and After School Clubs run during term time every day, with exception that After School Club does not run on the last day of each term which is used for audit and stock take.
Academic Year 2025/26 After School Club will not be available on the following dates:
Academic Year 2026/27 After School Club will not be available on the following dates:
Breakfast and After School Club is open to children of all ages across our school. It is not run by teachers so, for everyone’s enjoyment and safety, the expectation is that your child can independently use the toilet and able to listen to and follow instructions given to them. A copy of our behaviour policy is below and specifically references expectations for wrap around care. School reserve the right to refuse a place in this facility if deemed necessary.
Breakfast ClubThis runs each morning from 7.40am – 8.40am.
The school gate is open for 15 minutes between 7:40am – 7:55am. We request all children are dropped off within this time.
We offer a variety of breakfast options, which vary daily, and include cereal and toast. Activities include construction play and mindfulness colouring.
This club runs daily from 3.15pm – 5.45pm. Children are collected from their classrooms. They are offered a drink & healthy snack which includes freshly made crumpets, toasted fruit loaf, malt loaf & fresh fruit. There are a range of activities including arts and crafts, playdoh, board games and indoor and outdoor play.
Late collection after 5.45pm will incur a penalty charge of £5 for every 5 minutes.
Although the clubs are relaxed and a freer setting than during the school day all school policies, and our school values of love, hope and courage will still apply (see school website for policies).
There are two options for attending these clubs:
Registration forms must be completed before your child attends ASC. These can be collected from the school office along with a welcome pack.
Childcare vouchersWe accept the government Tax Free Childcare scheme and the Childcare Grant Payment Scheme for Breakfast and After School clubs. Please contact the office to set this up in the first instance.
All parents who require a permanent place for their child must complete a Permanent Place agreement form, which can be downloaded from our school website. On receipt of the form we will set up the permanent booking on Scopay. By signing the agreement you are agreeing to make regular payments via Scopay, if this is not the case your place may be withdrawn. A minimum notice period of 20 school days is required to cancel a permanent place. You will be liable for all fees due under the period of notice, even if your child stops attending, unless there is a child on the waiting list who requires this place. There will be no refunds for cancelled sessions.
SuspensionsAll adults and children have a right to feel safe and respected. The school has the right to refuse a child a place at the Breakfast or After School Care Club if a child’s behaviour is not in line with the school’s behaviour policy.
If your child’s behaviour warrants it due to poor behaviour choices, you will receive a behaviour notice. Three notices will result in a 10 day suspension from using this facility.
If you have any further questions please contact the School office.

The school uniform for boys and girls consists of:
PE uniform – children should come to school wearing their PE kit on PE days
The school P.E. uniform for boys and girls consists of:
Football kits and branded hoodies or tracksuits are not to be worn for P.E.

Schools Games Platinum School Mark
We are delighted to announce that at Nursling, we have achieved Schools Games Platinum School Mark.
The School Games Mark is a Government-led award scheme launched in 2012, facilitated by the Youth Sport Trust to reward schools for their commitment to the development of sports and competition across their school and into the community, and we are delighted to have been recognised for our success.
With our young people competing in local inter-school competitions this year, we are extremely proud of our pupils for their dedication to all aspects of school sport.
This is our first-time achieving platinum and we look forward to continuing next year. Thank you to everyone who has supported sports at Nursling. Well done team Nursling!

Parenting Pointers
We all function better when we get a good night’s sleep. Children ideally need 8 hours of sleep each night. Action for Children have good suggestions and advice on sleep.
How can you help to support your child? Maybe by: limiting time allowed on electronics, eating dinner together around a table, talking about the day, sharing a book or going for a walk. Always try to focus on the positives and never go to bed on an argument!

Our school lunches are provided by Aspens, who specialise in catering for the education sector, provide hot lunches for our children. Pupil Premium
Pupil Premium Report 2025 2026
At Nursling C of E Primary School, we have high aspirations for every child and believe that all children can succeed. We strongly believe that every child can reach beyond their potential given the right learning environment and through high quality teaching which engages, inspires and deepens their knowledge and understanding of the world they live in. This together with the child’s dedication and commitment to learning as well as working with parents to ensure they are playing a vital role in supporting their child’s achievement.
The Pupil Premium funding is allocated to schools from the government to support children who may be vulnerable to underachievement. The funding is given to schools based on the number of pupils on roll known to be eligible for Free School Meals, or who have claimed in the last 6 years, as well as those who have been ‘Looked After’ by the local authority.
When making decisions about using pupil premium funding it is important to consider the context of the school and subsequent challenges faced. Common barriers for PPG children can be less support at home, home issues, weak language and communication skills, lack of confidence, more frequent behaviour difficulties, attendance and punctuality issues. There may be more complex family situations that prevent children from flourishing. The challenges are varied and there is no ‘one size fits all’.
Our pupil premium strategy has been put together based on data analysis and knowing our children and their families. A programme of support is then put into place in school to help our children to reach their full potential. This may involve strategies such as: working alongside other agencies, small group interventions, ELSA support and engaging parents.
